```{python}
#| label: representation-setup
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from live_results import *

DB = source_path("results/checkpoint_embeddings/compact.sqlite")
jobs = read_sql(DB, "select * from jobs order by job_id")
diagnostics = read_sql(DB, "select * from diagnostics")
extended = read_sql(DB, "select * from extended_results")
paired = read_sql(DB, "select * from paired_comparisons")
predictor = read_sql(DB, "select * from predictor_comparisons")
odds = read_sql(DB, "select * from odds_ratios")
multiclass = read_sql(DB, "select * from multiclass_results")
confusion = read_sql(DB, "select * from confusion_matrix")
records = read_sql(DB, "select * from records")
similarity = read_sql(DB, "select * from checkpoint_similarity")
stability = read_sql(DB, "select * from umap_stability")
multiplicity = read_sql(DB, "select * from multiplicity_results")

job_labels = jobs.set_index("job_id")["model_id"].to_dict()
for frame in (extended, predictor, odds, multiclass, diagnostics):
    frame["model_id"] = frame["job_id"].map(job_labels)
for frame in (paired, similarity):
    frame["model_a"] = frame["job_a"].map(job_labels)
    frame["model_b"] = frame["job_b"].map(job_labels)

ANCHORS = ["factorial_ecg_aim_1000000_s42", "factorial_ecg_aim_1011011_s42"]
confusion["model_id"] = confusion["job_id"].map(job_labels)

def compact_ci(frame, digits=3):
    out = frame.copy()
    out["estimate (95% CI)"] = out.apply(
        lambda r: f"{r.value:.{digits}f} [{r.ci_low:.{digits}f}, {r.ci_high:.{digits}f}]"
        if pd.notna(r.ci_low) and pd.notna(r.ci_high) else f"{r.value:.{digits}f}", axis=1)
    return out
```

## What question this study can answer

This is a **frozen-representation audit**, not another reconstruction
leaderboard. It asks whether a frozen ECG-AIM encoder contains linearly
accessible rhythm-code or annotation-timing information; whether that
information adds to deliberately small waveform controls; whether `1011011`
improves on the raw `1000000` anchor on the same records; and whether latent
outliers are associated with reconstruction failure.

The rhythm endpoint is released cross-sectional code membership. The timing
endpoint is the annotation interval from QRS onset to T offset; it is explicitly
**not clinical QT or QTc**. Neither endpoint establishes diagnosis, prospective
AF prediction, causal physiology, or identifiability of a missing 12-lead ECG.

::: {.callout-important}
## Bottom line

The latents contain useful rhythm-code information, but the current experiment
does not show that `1011011` is a better AF representation than `1000000`.
`1011011` improves several measures of annotation-interval encoding, while
direct waveform summaries remain substantially better for absolute timing.
Rhythm codes are locally enriched in latent space but not globally separated.
:::

## Completion, split scope, and leakage boundary

```{python}
#| label: representation-jobs
display(source_inventory({"checkpoint representation DB": DB}))
display(jobs[["model_id", "split_scope", "expected_records", "completed_records",
              "feature_dim", "status", "checkpoint_sha256"]])
display(jobs.groupby(["split_scope", "status"])
        .agg(jobs=("job_id", "nunique"), records=("completed_records", "sum"),
             dimensions=("feature_dim", "unique")).reset_index())
```

All 11 extraction jobs are complete. Only the two anchors have train,
validation, and test activations. Their probes were selected on validation data
and evaluated once on shared test records. The other nine checkpoints are
test-only and contribute geometry, similarity, and visualization—not fitted
probes. Fitting probes on them would leak the evaluation split.

The pipeline standardizes and fits PCA on training data, restricts probes to at
most eight PCA components, applies a validation one-standard-error selection
rule favouring simpler candidates, and refits on train plus validation. Test
intervals use paired record-level bootstrap resamples. These safeguards do not
remove single-split or single-seed uncertainty.

## Binary AF/AFIB code-membership probe

The waveform comparator contains heart rate, signal RMS, and spectral entropy.
It is interpretable but intentionally small; it is **not** a strong native-ECG
classifier. Beating it demonstrates incremental information relative to three
summaries, not clinical superiority.

```{python}
#| label: af-probe-table
af = extended[(extended.outcome == "AF_AFIB_code_membership") &
              (extended.metric.isin(["auroc", "auprc", "brier", "log_loss"])) &
              (extended.model_id.isin(ANCHORS))].copy()
af = compact_ci(af)
display(af[["model_id", "predictor_set", "metric", "estimate (95% CI)", "n"]]
        .sort_values(["model_id", "predictor_set", "metric"]))

af_plot = af[af.metric.isin(["auroc", "auprc"])].copy()
fig = px.bar(af_plot, x="predictor_set", y="value", color="model_id",
             facet_col="metric", barmode="group",
             error_y=af_plot.ci_high-af_plot.value,
             error_y_minus=af_plot.value-af_plot.ci_low,
             labels={"value": "held-out estimate", "predictor_set": "predictor"})
fig.update_layout(title="Held-out AF/AFIB code discrimination")
fig.show()
```

For `1000000`, latent AUROC is 0.760 (95% CI 0.710–0.812), compared with
0.713 (0.654–0.766) for waveform summaries; the combined model reaches 0.788
(0.737–0.836). For `1011011`, latent AUROC is 0.787 (0.740–0.836), and the
combined model reaches 0.794 (0.746–0.841). Both anchors therefore encode
rhythm-associated information. Whether the enhanced objective caused an
improvement requires the paired anchor contrast below.

### Probe selection, prevalence, and calibration

```{python}
#| label: af-probe-specification
selection_source = extended[
    (extended.outcome == "AF_AFIB_code_membership") &
    (extended.metric == "auroc") &
    (extended.model_id.isin(ANCHORS))
].copy()
selection_details = json_normalize(selection_source.details_json, prefix="")
selection_table = pd.concat([
    selection_source[["model_id", "predictor_set", "n"]].reset_index(drop=True),
    selection_details[["dims", "C", "validation_loss", "validation_loss_se",
                       "validation_calibration_intercept",
                       "validation_calibration_slope", "selection"]]
], axis=1)
display(selection_table)

calibration = extended[
    (extended.outcome == "AF_AFIB_code_membership") &
    (extended.metric.isin(["calibration_intercept", "calibration_slope",
                           "predicted_risk_IQR_contrast"])) &
    (extended.model_id.isin(ANCHORS))
]
display(calibration[["model_id", "predictor_set", "metric", "value", "n"]]
        .sort_values(["model_id", "predictor_set", "metric"]))
display(records.query("split == 'test'").canonical_rhythm.value_counts()
        .rename_axis("released canonical code").reset_index(name="records"))
```

The held-out set contains 120 AF/AFIB-coded and 240 other records. AUROC is not
prevalence-dependent, but AUPRC must be interpreted against the 0.333 no-skill
prevalence. The calibrated probes all select `C=0.01`; waveform uses three
features and latent/combined probes use eight PCA dimensions. Strong shrinkage
and low dimension make this closer to a linear-accessibility test than a large
downstream classifier.

Test calibration slopes are 1.17–1.24 for latent-only and 1.10–1.15 for the
combined probes, with intercepts near zero. This is reasonable internal
calibration after validation adjustment, not external calibration. The
`1011011` latent produces a larger interquartile predicted-risk contrast
(0.302) than waveform summaries (0.186), but risk spread is not clinical net
benefit.

The older `probe_results` table stores a superseded uncalibrated analysis with
different selected regularization. This chapter consistently uses
`extended_results` and its paired tables; mixing generations would change the
estimand silently.

### Incremental information relative to waveform controls

```{python}
#| label: af-predictor-contrasts
af_predictor = predictor[predictor.outcome == "AF_AFIB_code_membership"].copy()
af_predictor["contrast"] = af_predictor.reference_set + " → " + af_predictor.candidate_set
display(af_predictor[["model_id", "contrast", "metric",
                      "delta_candidate_minus_reference", "ci_low", "ci_high", "p_value"]]
        .sort_values(["model_id", "contrast", "metric"]))
display(odds[odds.outcome == "AF_AFIB_code_membership"]
        [["model_id", "predictor_set", "odds_ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high",
          "p_value", "events", "total"]])
```

For `1011011`, latent versus waveform improves AUROC by 0.0738
(95% CI 0.0157–0.1345; Holm-adjusted *p*=0.011) and reduces Brier score by
0.0231 (Holm-adjusted *p*=0.002). Adding latent features to waveform summaries
improves AUROC by 0.0801 and AUPRC by 0.0788. Once the latent is present, adding
the waveform summaries changes AUROC by only 0.0063 (CI crosses zero).

For `1000000`, latent-versus-waveform AUROC and AUPRC intervals cross zero,
although Brier score and log loss improve. Its combined model is consistently
better than waveform alone. The defensible claim is **incremental rhythm-code
information, with stronger evidence for probability quality than for a large
discrimination gain**. Per-SD probe-score odds ratios near 3 are associations,
not causal risks or prospective recurrence effects.

## Does `1011011` beat the raw anchor?

```{python}
#| label: paired-anchor-comparison
paired_show = paired.copy()
paired_show["contrast"] = paired_show.model_a + " → " + paired_show.model_b
display(paired_show[["contrast", "outcome", "metric", "delta_b_minus_a",
                     "ci_low", "ci_high", "p_value"]]
        .sort_values(["outcome", "metric"]))
```

For AF/AFIB code membership, `1011011 − 1000000` gives AUROC +0.0270
(95% CI −0.0227 to +0.0760; *p*=0.329), AUPRC −0.0283 (*p*=0.610), Brier
−0.0034 (*p*=0.682), and log loss −0.0055 (*p*=0.804). Every interval includes
no difference. The data permit a small loss or moderate gain; calling
`1011011` an improved AF base architecture would overstate the evidence.

## Annotation-defined QRS-onset–to–T-offset timing

```{python}
#| label: timing-probe-table
timing = extended[(extended.outcome == "annotation_QRSon_Toff_ms") &
                  (extended.metric.isin(["mae_ms", "rmse_ms", "r2", "pearson",
                                         "spearman", "lin_ccc"])) &
                  (extended.model_id.isin(ANCHORS))].copy()
timing = compact_ci(timing)
display(timing[["model_id", "predictor_set", "metric", "estimate (95% CI)", "n"]]
        .sort_values(["model_id", "predictor_set", "metric"]))

timing_delta = predictor[predictor.outcome == "annotation_QRSon_Toff_ms"].copy()
timing_delta["contrast"] = timing_delta.reference_set + " → " + timing_delta.candidate_set
display(timing_delta[["model_id", "contrast", "metric",
                      "delta_candidate_minus_reference", "ci_low", "ci_high", "p_value"]]
        .sort_values(["model_id", "contrast", "metric"]))
```

The mean-only MAE is 44.76 ms. Waveform summaries reduce it to 22.53 ms. The
latent-only MAE is 38.21 ms for `1000000` and 35.79 ms for `1011011`; both are
substantially worse than waveform features. Adding either latent to waveform
changes MAE by less than 0.24 ms, with intervals crossing zero. The latent does
not add convincing absolute-timing utility beyond the waveform summaries.

The matched anchor contrast is more favourable: `1011011` reduces latent-only
RMSE by 4.02 ms (95% CI 1.39–6.60; *p*=0.005), increases Spearman correlation
by 0.109 (*p*=0.012), and increases Lin's concordance by 0.108 (*p*=0.003).
Its 2.42-ms MAE improvement narrowly includes zero (*p*=0.051). This supports
better encoding of the annotation interval—not replacement of waveform timing
and not a QT/QTc claim.

## Multiclass rhythm probe: broad signal, weak resolution

```{python}
#| label: multiclass-probe
macro = compact_ci(multiclass[(multiclass.model_id.isin(ANCHORS)) &
                              (multiclass.class_label == "__macro__")])
display(macro[["model_id", "metric", "estimate (95% CI)", "n"]]
        .sort_values(["model_id", "metric"]))

per_class = multiclass[(multiclass.model_id.isin(ANCHORS)) &
                       (~multiclass.class_label.str.startswith("__")) &
                       (multiclass.metric.isin(["sensitivity", "specificity",
                                                "ovr_auroc", "ovr_auprc"]))]
display(per_class.pivot_table(index=["model_id", "class_label"],
                              columns="metric", values="value").reset_index())

for model_id in ANCHORS:
    cm = confusion[confusion.model_id == model_id].pivot(
        index="true_label", columns="predicted_label", values="row_fraction").fillna(0)
    fig = px.imshow(cm, text_auto=".2f", zmin=0, zmax=1,
                    color_continuous_scale="Blues",
                    labels={"x": "predicted code", "y": "true code",
                            "color": "row fraction"},
                    title=f"Held-out multiclass confusion: {model_id}")
    fig.show()
```

The enhanced anchor descriptively improves macro AUROC from 0.687 to 0.743 and
macro F1 from 0.239 to 0.284, but balanced accuracy remains only 0.302. This is
not an eight-class rhythm solution. Rare-code results are exploratory at 360
test records and must be shown class by class rather than summarized by the
more flattering macro AUROC.

The test composition is deliberately uneven: AF, AFIB, SA, SB, and SR each
have 60 records, while AT has 18 and ST/SVT have 21 each. The row-normalized
confusion matrices show whether macro changes arise from common or rare codes.
Specificity can remain high for a rare one-versus-rest class despite poor
sensitivity, so neither specificity nor macro AUROC is sufficient alone.

## Reconstruction-failure probe

```{python}
#| label: failure-probe
display(odds[odds.outcome == "reconstruction_failure"]
        [["model_id", "predictor_set", "odds_ratio", "ci_low", "ci_high",
          "p_value", "events", "total", "details_json"]])
```

For the checkpoint-matched enhanced anchor, a one-SD increase in latent outlier
score is associated with 2.15-fold higher odds of the stored reconstruction
failure definition (95% CI 1.40–3.30; Holm-adjusted *p*=0.0013; 24 failures
among 360 records). The threshold was fixed on validation data and tested once,
making this stronger than a post-hoc UMAP observation. The event count remains
small and the endpoint is model QC, not patient prognosis. Its plausible use is
abstention or review prioritisation after external calibration.

## High-dimensional geometry versus UMAP appearance

```{python}
#| label: representation-geometry
high_dim = diagnostics[(diagnostics.analysis == "rigorous_high_dim") &
                       (diagnostics.split == "test")]
display(high_dim[["model_id", "metric", "value", "details_json"]]
        .sort_values(["metric", "model_id"]))
display(multiplicity[multiplicity.family == "representation_label_nulls"]
        [["hypothesis", "raw_p", "adjusted_p", "method"]]
        .sort_values("adjusted_p"))
display(similarity[["model_a", "model_b", "split", "metric", "value"]]
        .sort_values(["split", "metric", "model_a", "model_b"]))
display(stability.groupby(["job_id", "metric"])["value"]
        .agg(["count", "mean", "std", "min", "max"]).reset_index()
        .merge(jobs[["job_id", "model_id"]], on="job_id", how="left"))
```

All 11 checkpoints show significant 10-nearest-neighbour rhythm-code agreement
after Benjamini–Hochberg correction, with agreement around 0.18–0.24. In
contrast, every high-dimensional rhythm silhouette is negative and its
permutation test is non-significant. These are compatible: codes are locally
enriched without forming clean global clusters. A visually separated UMAP is
therefore not proof of discrete rhythm manifolds.

## Multiplicity and claim ledger

```{python}
#| label: multiplicity-ledger
display(multiplicity.sort_values(["family", "adjusted_p"]))
```

| Proposed statement | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Frozen ECG-AIM latents encode AF/AFIB-associated information | Supported within this split | Held-out probes discriminate code membership and improve probability scores over three waveform summaries. |
| The enhanced objective is superior for AF representation | Not supported | All paired AF anchor-comparison intervals include zero. |
| `1011011` better encodes QRS-onset–to–T-offset annotation timing | Partially supported | RMSE, rank correlation, and concordance improve; MAE is borderline. |
| Latents outperform direct waveform timing | Contradicted | Latent MAE is 13–16 ms worse; combined gains are negligible. |
| ECG-AIM creates globally separated rhythm clusters | Contradicted | Silhouettes are negative and permutation tests are non-significant. |
| Local latent neighbourhoods contain rhythm structure | Supported, exploratory | All kNN agreement tests survive BH correction. |
| Latent outlier score flags reconstruction failure | Supported internally | Held-out OR 2.15 per SD, but only 24 events and no external calibration. |
| These probes establish clinical utility | Not supported | Cross-sectional codes, one split, weak comparator, and no prospective endpoint. |

## What would change the conclusion

The highest-value follow-ups are repeated patient-level splits or external
cohorts; a strong native-waveform classifier comparator; predeclared probe
dimensionality; calibration and decision-curve analysis; external validation of
the failure score; and matched one-lead wavelet representations once
train/validation/test embeddings exist. Until then, this supports a
representation-mechanism and quality-control claim, not deployment.
